description: The A=3 count-channel carrier space collapses to a single integer M = m1+m2+m3, and is exhausted: b3/b2 = M - 3 is a non-negative integer while the measured ratio is 950815/1483044, strictly between 0 and 1. Every carrier misses by at least 532229/1483044 (55.98%), attained at M=4, and the gap grows monotonically beyond -- so the exclusion is complete over every crossing number. This closes the 'search the 20 triples' step by proving there is nothing to search.

collapse.step_1: countChannel depends only on n+ + n-, so 382,637,520 band words -> 20 triples at c <= 12
collapse.step_2: b3/b2 = M - 3 depends only on the SUM, so 20 triples -> 4 values of M

exhaustion.reason: b3/b2 = M - 3 increases with M, so nothing above M=4 can do better; c <= 12 was never a restriction

assertions.name: the measured ratio is the exact rational the Lean carries
assertions.detail: matches QOU.Mass.CarrierCrossingQuantisation.rMeasured, imported by the Lean rather than restated

assertions.name: b3 sees only the SUM -- the 20 triples collapse to 4 values of M
assertions.detail: 20 triples at c <= 12, 4 distinct M; every triple with the same sum gives the identical b3/b2 (Lean bRatio_depends_only_on_sum)

assertions.name: M = 3 is FORCED to be (1,1,1) -- the Borromean -- and gives exactly 0
assertions.detail: one clasp per pair is the only triple summing to 3; it lands exactly on the degenerate locus, agreeing with CountChannelCarrierLocus.canonical_carriers_b3_eq_zero -- reached here by exhaustion rather than by assignment

assertions.name: no integer M reproduces the measured b3
assertions.detail: b3/b2 = M - 3 is an integer; the measured value lies strictly between 0 and 1. The Lean proves it for EVERY integer, and does not even need the Brunnian hypothesis (no_carrier_reproduces_b3)

assertions.name: and every carrier misses by >= 532229/1483044 (55.98%), attained at M=4
assertions.detail: min gap 532229/1483044 = 0.358876, 55.98% of measured, at M = 4; matches the Lean bound carrier_gap_bounded_below

assertions.name: c <= 12 was NEVER a restriction -- the gap grows monotonically past M=4
assertions.detail: b3/b2 = M - 3 increases with M, so no larger carrier can do better (Lean gap_increases_beyond_four). The enumeration is complete over EVERY crossing number, not merely c <= 12 -- there is no larger search to run

scope: (b) on the conjunction {b3 carried by the count channel, mu ∝ c, Hopf pair carrier c2 = 2, Brunnian A=3 carrier}, invariant named: M is an integer >= 3, so b3/b2 is a non-negative integer while the measured ratio is not one. (a) on each ingredient separately -- it does NOT say the count channel is wrong nor that the carrier is not Brunnian; brunnian_binding_survives is untouched.
caveats: The live ingredient is the FIRST one -- that b3 is carried by the count channel at all. Owner ruling A fixes the pair carrier; dropping Brunnian-ness hits brunnian_not_pairLocal (a pair-local carrier forces b3 = 0, refuted by AME); and bRatio_scale_invariant shows mu ∝ c is not a convention one can relax. So the exclusion points back to qou-brng's original framing: the extensive term is somewhere the crossing count does not reach.
This is A=3 only. b4 and the A=4 carrier (6 pairs, not 3) are not touched, and nothing here follows for them.

b3 uses the isospin-averaged Bbar(3). A carrier assigning DIFFERENT triples to 3H and 3He would put b3/b2 on the half-integer grid rather than the integers -- that case is the one already covered by CarrierCrossingQuantisation.even_lattice_gap (22.01%), not by this file, and it is still excluded.
The Lean imports rMeasured from CarrierCrossingQuantisation rather than restating it, so the two cannot drift apart.
source: AME2020 total nuclear binding energies; integer crossing counts
